issue_context.body:
Static code scan issues found in file:

https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/tree/b1def7145fd/drivers/gpio/gpio_pca_series.c#L1544

Category: Uninitialized variables
Function: `gpio_pca_series_interrupt_handler_standard`
Component: Drivers

Details:

https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/b1def7145fd/drivers/gpio/gpio_pca_series.c#L1544

```
1538     #endif /* CONFIG_GPIO_PCA_SERIES_CACHE_ALL */
1539    
1540     out:
1541             k_sem_give(&data->lock);
1542

>>>     CID 434667:  Uninitialized variables  (UNINIT)
>>>     Using uninitialized value "input".
1544                     *input_value = input;
1545             }

1547                     gpio_fire_callbacks(&data->callbacks, dev, int_status);
```

For more information about the violation, check the [Coverity Reference](https://scan9.scan.coverity.com/doc/en/cov_checker_ref.html#static_checker_UNINIT). ([CWE-457](http://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/457.html))

https://scan9.scan.coverity.com/#/project-view/29271/12996?selectedIssue=434667

Note: This issue was created automatically. Priority was set based on classification
of the file affected and the impact field in coverity. Assignees were set using the MAINTAINERS file.

review_comments: It may not just this simple. `input` is assigned a value when `ret = gpio_pca_series_reg_read(dev, PCA_REG_TYPE_1B_INPUT_PORT, (uint8_t *)&input);` is called at #L1518. The error-checking go-to's can skip this assignment, leading to the issue. The better fix might be only run `if (input_value) { *input_value = input; }` when there's no error before reading the reg. If it gets an error before reading reg (this is FATAL anyways), the old input value should be kept as-is. My bad for not considering this.
Yeah you are right. this does not affect the input_old history value. I'm over concerned.
